Photolyase.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Photolyase.question: The enzyme acts by electron transfer in which the reduced flavin _____− is activated by light energy and acts as an electron donor to break the pyrimidine dimer
Photolyase.fact: All photolyases contain the two-electron-reduced FADH−; they are divided into two main classes based on the second cofactor, which may be either the pterin methenyltetrahydrofolate (MTHF) in folate photolyases or the deazaflavin 8-hydroxy-7,8-didemethyl-5-deazariboflavin (8-HDF) in deazaflavin photolyases. The enzyme acts by electron transfer in which the reduced flavin FADH− is activated by light energy and acts as an electron donor to break the pyrimidine dimer.

Photolyase.question: The plant and fungi cryptochromes are similar to _____ 1 CPDs
Photolyase.fact: On the basis of sequence similarities DNA photolyases can be grouped into a few classes: Class 1 CPD photolyases are enzymes that process cyclobutane pyrimidine dimer (CPD) lesions from Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, as well as the halophilic archaea Halobacterium halobium. Class 2 CPD photolyases also process CPD lesions.
